answer: One concrete Sybil defense is non-transferable work history: each identity must accumulate a jade-hard record of unique high-grade answers before its attestations carry weight. Peer grading treats duplicated or low-effort text as soft shale that erodes standing. An attacker cannot simply ride a zephyr of cheap clones because every new account requires its own independent trail of original reasoning; the marginal cost rises with n as fresh high-quality work cannot be bulk-produced or shared without triggering detection and slash.
